les: Van die winkel tot op jou bord
kaps_punt: Voedselhigiëne: Veilige en skadelike bestanddele; Voedselvoorbereiding; Voedselberging; Siektes wat deur voedsel oorgedra kan word.

items.bewering: Kos kan jou siek maak, al lyk dit reg op jou bord.
items.bron: SFDA FAQ (sfda.gov.sa/en/faq/do-spoilage-bacteria-make-people-sick, following USDA FSIS): pathogenic bacteria grow in the danger zone without generally changing the taste, smell or appearance of food; WSU Extension FSM 267 says the same.

items.bewering: Kieme is baie klein lewende dinge wat in kos kan groei.
items.bron: MSU Extension 'What are germs anyway?' and KidsHealth 'Germs': germs are microscopic living things (bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa) that can cause disease. Bacteria and moulds multiply in food (FSIS danger-zone release). Nuance for a person, not a fault: viruses cannot reproduce outside a host cell (KidsHealth), so they do not grow in food. The sentence uses 'kan' and does not say every germ grows in food, so it holds as written. 'Lewend' follows the CAPS usage the project kept.

items.bewering: Voedselhigiëne beteken dat jy kos so koop, voorberei en bêre dat kieme, gif en bederf niemand siek maak nie. Kortweg: jy hanteer kos veilig.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food (who.int/publications/i/item/9789241594639): food safety covers clean handling, separating raw and cooked, cooking thoroughly, safe storage temperatures and safe water and raw materials (buying, preparing, storing). On 'bederf' as a cause of illness: SFDA/USDA say most spoilage bacteria probably do not make a person sick, but FSIS 'Molds on Food' says poisonous substances (mycotoxins) are often in and around mould threads, so spoiled food can make a person ill. Holds as worded.

items.bewering: Bederfde kos ruik dikwels suur of sleg. Party kos kry 'n slymerige laag.
items.bron: SFDA FAQ (after USDA FSIS): spoilage bacteria make food mushy or slimy, or make meat smell bad.

items.bewering: Op ander kos groei 'n pluisige laag skimmel in kleure soos wit, groen, grys of swart.
items.bron: FSIS 'Molds on Food' (as summarised via fsis.usda.gov/es/node/3303) and a nutritionist in Daily Monitor (monitor.co.ug, 'How dangerous is mould on food?'): fuzzy spore colonies in white, yellow, green, grey or black.

items.bewering: Gooi sulke kos heeltemal weg en moenie net die skimmel afskraap nie.
items.bron: FSIS 'Molds on Food': mould roots grow deep into food and toxins may spread through it, so scraping the surface is not enough; soft and moist foods are discarded. FSIS lets a person cut a wide margin off hard cheese and firm vegetables. 'Throw it all away' is more cautious than FSIS but is safe advice for a child, and the claim that scraping is not enough is correct.

items.bewering: Moenie proe of kos bederf is nie.
items.bron: WSU Extension FSM 267 and SFDA FAQ: illness-causing bacteria do not change the taste, smell or look of food, so tasting cannot show whether food is safe. Monterey County botulism guidance: do not taste suspect food.

items.bewering: Jou neus en oë merk dikwels bederf op, maar gewoonlik nie die kieme wat jou siek maak nie.
items.bron: SFDA FAQ (after USDA FSIS): spoilage bacteria change smell and texture; pathogenic bacteria grow without generally changing taste, smell or appearance. WSU Extension FSM 267 agrees.

items.bewering: Rou vleis, hoender en eiers kan kieme dra. Maak hulle gaar totdat hulle binne-in ook heeltemal gaar is.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food: cook meat, poultry, eggs and seafood thoroughly (70 °C; juices clear, not pink). US state Salmonella fact sheets (e.g. Alaska DPH): raw or undercooked poultry and eggs are common sources.

items.bewering: Was vrugte en groente voordat jy dit eet.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food, key 5: wash fruits and vegetables, especially if eaten raw.

items.bewering: Moenie 'n blikkie oopmaak of daaruit proe as dit opgeswel is of lek nie. Wys dit vir 'n grootmens om weg te gooi.
items.bron: Monterey County Health, Botulism information: do not open or puncture suspect cans, and do not taste food from containers that leak, bulge or are swollen. Food Safety News (2013) summarises CDC guidance the same way.

items.bewering: Baie kosetikette het Engelse woorde voor die datum. 'Use by' ... 'Best before' ...
items.bron: Mail & Guardian, 21 Sep 2023, 'How food date labelling works': SA labels carry 'Best before' and 'Use by' written out in full; City of Cape Town, 'Food date labels are good for your health and wallet'.

items.bewering: 'Use by' wys die laaste dag waarop jy die kos mag eet.
items.bron: City of Cape Town, 'Food date labels...': 'Use By' is the most critical date, for perishable food such as meat and dairy (only food frozen by that date is safe later). A Mail & Guardian piece and an R146 summary (ASC Food Safety) call it the safety date for perishable food.

items.bewering: 'Best before' wys tot wanneer die kos op sy beste smaak. Ná daardie datum kan kos nog veilig wees as dit reg gebêre is.
items.bron: City of Cape Town, 'Food date labels...': most items past their best-before dates are still fine to eat if stored correctly. gov.za 2012 notice on R146: best-before relates to optimum freshness. BusinessTech: best before is the date up to which full quality can be enjoyed.

items.bewering: Die etiket het ook 'n lys van die bestanddele in die kos. Soek daarop na iets wat jou kan skaad, soos grondboontjies as jy daarvoor allergies is.
items.bron: Summaries of SA labelling regulation R146 (SGS Safeguards 043/12; SAWIS allergen memo): ingredients must be listed, and common allergens including peanuts must be declared.

items.bewering: Was jou hande met seep en water voordat jy aan kos raak. Was hulle weer nadat jy rou vleis of hoender vasgehou het. So dra jou hande nie kieme na brood of slaai nie.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food, keys 1 and 2: wash hands before handling food and often during preparation; microbes move from hands and utensils onto food; keep raw meat and poultry apart from other foods.

items.bewering: Hou rou vleis apart van kos wat klaar is om te eet. Gebruik 'n aparte snyplank en mes daarvoor, of was hulle met warm seepwater.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food, key 2: use separate knives and cutting boards for raw foods; key 1: wash and sanitise surfaces and equipment used for food.

items.bewering: Was en kook kos net met skoon water.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food, key 5: use safe water, or treat it to make it safe.

items.bewering: Kos soos vleis, melk en gaar kos bederf vinnig as dit warm staan. Hou sulke kos koel, in 'n yskas as daar een is.
items.bron: USDA FSIS press release 'USDA urges consumers to keep clear of the danger zone this summer': perishable food spoils rapidly between 40 and 140 °F. WHO Five Keys, key 4: refrigerate cooked and perishable food promptly (preferably below 5 °C).

items.bewering: Laat gaar kos nie langer as twee uur uit die yskas staan nie, of een uur op 'n baie warm dag.
items.bron: USDA FSIS danger-zone press release: no more than two hours in the danger zone, and one hour when it is above 90 °F (about 32 °C). WHO Five Keys: do not leave cooked food at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

items.bewering: Maak kos toe sodat vlieë nie kieme daarop agterlaat nie.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food, key 1: protect kitchen areas and food from insects, pests and other animals, because they carry microorganisms.

items.bewering: Bêre droë kos soos mieliemeel en rys in houers met 'n deksel. Dan kom muise en insekte nie so maklik daarby nie.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food, key 1: keep food in covered containers and protect it from insects, pests and other animals.

items.bewering: Hou gif en skoonmaakgoed ver van kos af en nooit in 'n kosbottel nie.
items.bron: City of Cape Town, 'Paraffin safety in the home': never store paraffin in used milk or cooldrink bottles. A Tygerberg Poison Centre doctor (quoted on motoring.co.za) says children mistake paraffin in cooldrink bottles for a drink.

items.bewering: Maak net soveel kos as wat julle gaan eet. Eet dit terwyl dit vars en warm is. Wat oorbly, mag ook net twee uur staan of een uur op 'n baie warm dag.
items.bron: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food, key 4: cooked food may not stand at room temperature for more than 2 hours, so where food cannot be cooled, eat it while hot. USDA FSIS danger-zone release: one hour above 90 °F.

items.bewering: Siekte van kos met kieme, gif of bederf daarin noem ons voedselvergiftiging.
items.bron: NHS 'Food poisoning': illness from eating contaminated food. 'Gif' is supported by NHS (something poisonous swallowed) and by FSIS on mould mycotoxins. 'Bederf' holds as worded: SFDA/USDA say spoilage bacteria usually do not make a person sick, but mouldy, spoiled food can carry toxins and pathogens (FSIS 'Molds on Food'; TODAY food-safety experts). The 'Vars of bederf?' block already keeps spoilage and the germs that make you sick apart.

items.bewering: Die gewone tekens en simptome is naarheid, maagkrampe, opgooi, diarree en soms koors. 'n Siek mens kry hulle nie noodwendig almal nie.
items.bron: NHS 'Food poisoning': feeling sick, being sick, diarrhoea, tummy pain, a high temperature. Salmonella fact sheets: fever is common, and nausea and vomiting are less frequent, so not everyone has every symptom.

items.bewering: Roep dadelik 'n grootmens as jy of iemand anders so siek word.
items.bron: This is advice, not a fact. It is consistent with NHS 'Food poisoning' guidance on when to get help.

items.bewering: As dit dalk gif is, neem die grootmens die siek mens met die houer dadelik kliniek toe.
items.bron: MedlinePlus/health-library 'First aid: poisoning': if hospital care is needed, take the container or poison along. NHS: go straight for urgent care if something poisonous may have been swallowed. The SA poison helpline (0861 555 777, Tygerberg/UCT) is not mentioned; the lesson does not need it and is not wrong without it.

items.bewering: Moenie vir tekens en simptome wag of hom laat opgooi nie.
items.bron: City of Cape Town 'Paraffin safety in the home': do not make a child who swallowed paraffin vomit, and get medical help quickly. MedlinePlus 'First aid: poisoning': do not make the person vomit, and get help at once.

items.bewering: By kieme of bederf is daar 'n groot gevaar dat die liggaam te veel water verloor. Bly klein slukkies water drink.
items.bron: NHS 'Food poisoning': drink lots of fluids to avoid dehydration and take small sips if you feel sick. Salmonella fact sheets: severe dehydration is the main risk.

items.bewering: As die siek mens nie water kan inhou nie of baie lomerig of swak word, neem 'n grootmens hom dadelik kliniek toe.
items.bron: NHS 'Food poisoning': get help urgently if the person keeps being sick and cannot keep fluids down, or is confused or not responding as usual. WHO IMCI general danger signs (WHO IMCI assessment booklet): unable to drink, vomits everything, lethargic or unconscious.

items.bewering: Dieselfde geld by moeilike asemhaling, stuiptrekkings of bloed in die diarree of opgooisel.
items.bron: NHS 'Food poisoning': bloody diarrhoea, blood in vomit and difficulty breathing need urgent help. WHO IMCI general danger signs: convulsions.

items.bewering: Word die siek mens nie beter nie, gaan hy ook kliniek toe.
items.bron: NHS 'Food poisoning': get help if diarrhoea lasts more than 7 days or vomiting more than 2 days.

items.bewering: Salmonellose en listeriose is twee soorte voedselvergiftiging wat van kieme kom.
items.bron: Salmonellosis is caused by Salmonella bacteria and listeriosis by Listeria monocytogenes; both are foodborne (US state fact sheets: Alaska DPH Salmonellosis; Wisconsin DHS and Pennsylvania DOH Listeriosis). Listeriosis is often invasive and more serious than ordinary food poisoning, but calling it a foodborne illness from germs is correct.

items.bewering: Salmonellose kan kom van hoender en eiers wat nie heeltemal gaar is nie.
items.bron: Alaska DPH Salmonellosis fact sheet: raw or undercooked poultry and eggs are common sources.

items.bewering: Listeriose kan kom van kos soos polonie, sagte kaas of rou melk.
items.bron: Polony: NICD outbreak investigation 2017-18 traced to Enterprise polony (Bhekisisa, 4 Mar 2018; Food Safety News, Apr 2018; 85% of interviewed cases had eaten ready-to-eat processed meat, mostly polony). Soft cheese and raw milk: Wisconsin DHS and Iowa HHS listeriosis fact sheets.

items.bewering: voedselhigiëne: Kos so koop, voorberei en bêre dat kieme, gif en bederf niemand siek maak nie.
items.bron: Same as the study block: WHO Five Keys to Safer Food; FSIS 'Molds on Food' for spoiled food that can make a person ill.

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak.
items.bron: MSU Extension 'What are germs anyway?'; KidsHealth 'Germs': microscopic organisms that can cause disease.

items.bewering: bederf: Wanneer kos sleg word, dikwels omdat kieme of skimmel daarin groei. Die kos ruik dan sleg, word slymerig of kry skimmel.
items.bron: SFDA FAQ (after USDA FSIS): spoilage bacteria make food slimy or mushy and give it a bad smell; FSIS 'Molds on Food'.

items.bewering: Bederf kan binne ure gebeur as kos warm staan.
items.bron: USDA FSIS danger-zone press release: perishable food spoils rapidly between 40 and 140 °F, and the safe limit is two hours (one above 90 °F).

items.bewering: skimmel: 'n Lewende groeisel wat ook op kos groei. Jy sien die pluisige deel in kleure soos wit, groen, grys of swart, maar sy dun drade groei in die kos in.
items.bron: FSIS 'Molds on Food' (fsis.usda.gov/es/node/3303): moulds are fungi with branches and roots like very thin threads that can grow deep into food and are hard to see; colours as in the Daily Monitor source above.

items.bewering: bestanddele: Al die dinge wat gebruik is om 'n kos te maak.
items.bron: R146 summaries (SGS Safeguards 043/12): the label's ingredient list names every ingredient by descending mass, which matches 'everything used to make the food'.

items.bewering: voedselvergiftiging: Siekte wat 'n mens kry van kos met kieme, gif of bederf daarin.
items.bron: Same as the 'Siek van kos' study item: NHS 'Food poisoning'; FSIS 'Molds on Food'; SFDA FAQ nuance on spoilage bacteria.

items.bewering: salmonellose: 'n Siekte wat deur kieme veroorsaak word en wat 'n mens byvoorbeeld kan kry van hoender of eiers wat nie heeltemal gaar is nie.
items.bron: Alaska DPH Salmonellosis fact sheet.

items.bewering: listeriose: 'n Siekte wat deur kieme veroorsaak word en wat 'n mens byvoorbeeld kan kry van polonie, sagte kaas of rou melk.
items.bron: NICD 2017-18 outbreak investigation (Bhekisisa; Food Safety News); Wisconsin DHS listeriosis fact sheet.

items.bewering: simptoom: Iets wat wys dat 'n mens se gesondheid skeefloop en wat hy self ervaar, soos pyn, moegheid of naarheid.
items.bron: Medical News Today 'Signs and symptoms' (medicalnewstoday.com/articles/161858): symptoms are subjective and felt by the person, e.g. pain or nausea.

items.bewering: teken: Iets wat wys dat 'n mens se gesondheid skeefloop en wat 'n ander mens self kan sien, hoor, ruik of meet, ook al vertel hy niks, soos 'n uitslag of koors.
items.bron: Medical News Today 'Signs and symptoms': signs are objective and can be noticed by people other than the patient; a rash and a fever are given as signs.

items.bewering: kliniek: 'n Plek in die gemeenskap waar mense gesondheidsorg kry, of hulle siek is of gesond.
items.bron: GCIS SA Yearbook 2004 health chapter and a UCT/Stellenbosch study (health.uct.ac.za): public PHC clinics give free preventive services (immunisation, family planning, antenatal care) as well as curative care.

opsomming: All 48 checkable claims hold against sources: no superlatives, no analogies and nothing contradicted or uncertain. Two points for a person, neither a fault: the sentence about germs that grow in food does not hold for viruses but does not claim every germ; and listing spoilage as a cause of food poisoning holds because mould toxins can make a person sick, although agencies say spoilage bacteria themselves usually do not.
